payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, can the source-image paper and cup be identified, and is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup without the paper already being stuffed inside?
node.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides enough evidence to identify the same paper and cup shown in the source, shows movement or placement advancing the paper toward or into the cup, and s1 has not established completion. Fail only if both objects are identifiable and there is visibly no progress toward the requested placement, or s1 establishes completion. Unknown if either object's identity or the relevant progress relation cannot be established.
node.binding: Progress counts only when it advances stuffing the source-image paper into the source-image cup. Do not infer absence of progress from uncertain object identity or proximity.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper and a blue cup, but the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a reddish object. The source paper and cup cannot be reliably identified in the edited image, so progress toward stuffing the paper into the cup cannot be established.

fulfillment: The node already encodes the key rubric distinction—completion, progress, and unresolved evidence—so do not relax those criteria to force the reference label. The trace is valid uncertainty, not a transport or schema failure: both supports were queried successfully, but their evidence does not establish object identity or progress. Improve the binding/evidence guidance so the checks compare the source and edited images for plausible continuity of the specific paper and cup, while allowing appearance changes when visual context supports identity. In these images, the source has a white sheet and blue cup; the edit shows a hand-held blue printed item near a reddish object. That mismatch makes identity uncertain, but the hand-held item could still be the paper and the reddish object could be the cup, so it is not affirmative evidence that no requested change progressed. Keep uncertainty available unless the visual evidence actually rules out progress; do not treat low confidence or repeated uncertainty as proof of absence. Ensure the completion and partial-progress supports assess their distinct criteria, and that the aggregate returns “no” only when both completion and progress are affirmatively ruled out under the rubric.
